The Key to the Bronte Works is a study by John Malham Dembleby, published in London in nineteen eleven. Its full title promises the key to Charlotte Bronte's Wuthering Heights, Jane Eyre, and her other works. It claims to show the method of their construction and their relation to facts and people of her life. An outline of Charlotte's life opens the chapters.

Later chapters hunt the origin of set scenes and figures, from a candle bearing night visitor to the foundling Heathcliff and his name. An insane lady and a white veil scene are traced in the same way. Dembleby reads the novels as coded life records. Bronte fans get a bold, disputed set of keys.

Neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore returns to Danny Jones with a new DMT study he says points to a parallel world. The episode title calls the study proof of a parallel dimension. Gallimore studies how the drug builds a world in the mind.

Gallimore lays out the new tests and what users saw when the drug was fed in slow doses. He argues the shared world they found is too rich to be mere noise. Jones asks what would prove the world is real and not made by the brain. Listeners get the latest from the lab edge. The library files the talk as an archive record.
